concepts.heading: Your Relationship Philosophy
concepts.alt: A guide standing at a lookout point holding a compass and gazing at the horizon
concepts.plain: After all you have learned, it is time to decide what you believe about relationships.

concepts.heading: What Is a Relationship Philosophy?
concepts.alt: A guide holding a compass in one hand and setting down a rulebook with the other
concepts.plain: It is a guide for your choices, not a list of rules.

concepts.heading: Key Questions for Your Philosophy
concepts.alt: A guide sorting cards that show a heart, a key, a wing and a shield
concepts.plain: Ask what you value most: honesty, freedom, safety, growth, fun?

concepts.heading: A Living Document
concepts.alt: A guide editing a page with a pencil and eraser, a small plant on the desk
concepts.plain: It will change over time, and that is fine.

concepts.heading: Shaped by History
concepts.alt: A guide looking thoughtfully through an old family photo album
concepts.plain: Your early life shaped your views. Check whether they still fit you.

options: Not a list of rules or a rigid manifesto
checks.explanation: Not a list of rules or a rigid manifesto. A relationship philosophy is not a list of rules or a rigid manifesto.

checks.prompt: Will your relationship philosophy stay the same forever?
options: Yes, once written it is fixed
checks.explanation: No, it will change. Your relationship philosophy will change. It is a living document.

3fb85402-a554-4c70-a03c-d57008224d5b.takeaway: Write down what you value in relationships and let it change as you grow.

concepts.heading: Your Growth Edge
concepts.alt: A guide standing at the edge of a ledge, looking excitedly at the next ledge
concepts.plain: Your growth edge is the spot where your skills meet your next challenge.

concepts.heading: Identifying Your Growth Edge
concepts.alt: A guide holding a glowing spark in his palm, curious
concepts.plain: Notice which topics in this course felt most alive for you. Start there.

concepts.heading: Setting Intentions, Not Resolutions
concepts.alt: A guide holding a compass and pointing ahead
concepts.plain: An intention is a direction to move in, not a pass-or-fail goal.

concepts.heading: Building Your Support Network
concepts.alt: Four guides linking arms in a row
concepts.plain: Nobody grows alone. Build a circle of people who support you.

concepts.heading: Self-Compassion Throughout Growth
concepts.alt: A guide dusting himself off after a stumble with a kind smile
concepts.plain: Progress goes up and down. Be kind to yourself.

concepts.heading: A Closing Affirmation
concepts.plain: You have put real time into understanding yourself. That counts.

options: A direction you want to move in
checks.explanation: A direction you want to move in. An intention is a direction you want to move in. A resolution is a rigid goal with pass/fail outcomes.
Not linear. Progress is not linear. You will have setbacks, moments of confusion, and times when old patterns reassert themselves.

ba522c3f-975e-4e68-afea-5e84176b3d1a.takeaway: Pick the one area you most want to grow in, set a direction, find support and be kind to yourself.

concepts.heading: The Power of Modeling Over Telling
concepts.alt: B picking up litter while C behind him starts doing the same
concepts.plain: People follow what you do, not what you say.

concepts.heading: The Nervous System as Leadership Instrument
concepts.alt: A guide conducting calmly with a baton, a smooth wave line flowing from her chest
concepts.plain: Your own calm body is your main tool for leading.

checks.after: The Power of Modeling Over Telling
options: What you do, not what you say
checks.explanation: What you do, not what you say. People don't follow what you say. They follow what you model.

checks.after: The Nervous System as Leadership Instrument
checks.prompt: What is your primary leadership tool?
checks.explanation: Your nervous system. Your nervous system is your primary leadership tool.

5439ca64-c711-4ed1-acb0-ad1cbfc17cf2.takeaway: Your calm is contagious. Regulate yourself first and show people instead of telling them.

concepts.heading: Creating Psychological Safety in Relationships
concepts.alt: A sharing something from the heart while B listens with an open, relaxed posture
concepts.plain: Safety in love means you can say a need without your partner getting defensive.

concepts.heading: Leadership During Conflict
concepts.alt: A guide standing steady like a tree in a strong wind
concepts.plain: Conflict is the real test of how you lead.

concepts.heading: Creating Containers for Difficult Conversations
concepts.alt: Two guides sitting and talking inside a circle of small candles
concepts.plain: Set up a safe time and place for the hard conversations.

43d57759-13a2-4b7b-95c0-1a6bfb79dc62.takeaway: Make it safe to be honest, stay steady in conflict, and repair after a rupture.

concepts.heading: The Paradox of Change: You Don't Change Others
concepts.alt: A guide lighting her own lantern while others nearby notice and light theirs
concepts.plain: You cannot change another person by force.

concepts.heading: Extending Leadership to Your Community
concepts.alt: Four guides walking out of a house into a neighbourhood, waving to neighbours
concepts.plain: The way you lead spreads from your relationships into your community.

checks.after: The Paradox of Change: You Don't Change Others
checks.prompt: What is the paradox of change?
options: You cannot change another person through willpower, persuasion or force
checks.explanation: You cannot change another person through willpower, persuasion or force. Here's the paradox: You cannot change another person through willpower, persuasion, or force.

checks.prompt: Where does embodied leadership naturally extend?
checks.explanation: Into your broader community. Embodied leadership naturally extends beyond your immediate relationships into your broader community.

6e7f49b2-31b6-42bb-9eb9-fd09e1a1c30c.takeaway: You cannot force anyone to change. Change yourself, and others often follow.
